Let $L_x,L_y>0$, let $N_x,N_y$ be integers at least $2$, and set $h_x=L_x/N_x$ and $h_y=L_y/N_y$. The rectangular grid nodes are $(x_i,y_j)=(ih_x,jh_y)$ for $0\le i\le N_x$ and $0\le j\le N_y$. The interior index set is $I_h=\{(i,j):1\le i<N_x,\ 1\le j<N_y\}$, and its boundary is the set of grid nodes with $i\in\{0,N_x\}$ or $j\in\{0,N_y\}$. A grid function is a real-valued function on all grid nodes; $X_{h,0}$ is the vector space of grid functions that vanish on the boundary.

For real vectors $v,w$ indexed by $I_h$, define the weighted interior inner product and norm by
$$
\langle v,w\rangle_h=h_xh_y\sum_{i=1}^{N_x-1}\sum_{j=1}^{N_y-1}v_{ij}w_{ij},\qquad \|v\|_h=\langle v,v\rangle_h^{1/2}.
$$
For full grid functions, the same notation applies to their restrictions to $I_h$; it gives a semidefinite bilinear form and a seminorm on all grid functions, and an inner product and norm on $X_{h,0}$.

The edge differences are $D_xv_{i+1/2,j}=(v_{i+1,j}-v_{ij})/h_x$ for $0\le i<N_x$, $1\le j<N_y$, and $D_yv_{i,j+1/2}=(v_{i,j+1}-v_{ij})/h_y$ for $1\le i<N_x$, $0\le j<N_y$. For a scalar coefficient $a$ sampled at face midpoints, write $a_{i+1/2,j}=a(x_i+h_x/2,y_j)$ and $a_{i,j+1/2}=a(x_i,y_j+h_y/2)$.

The positive divergence-form Dirichlet operator on interior nodes is
$$
(A_h^av)_{ij}=-\frac{a_{i+1/2,j}D_xv_{i+1/2,j}-a_{i-1/2,j}D_xv_{i-1/2,j}}{h_x}-\frac{a_{i,j+1/2}D_yv_{i,j+1/2}-a_{i,j-1/2}D_yv_{i,j-1/2}}{h_y}.
$$
For $a\equiv1$, this is the five-point Dirichlet Laplacian $-D_x^+D_x^- -D_y^+D_y^-$. The associated edge energy is
$$
E_h^a(v,w)=h_xh_y\left(\sum_{j=1}^{N_y-1}\sum_{i=0}^{N_x-1}a_{i+1/2,j}D_xv_{i+1/2,j}D_xw_{i+1/2,j}+\sum_{i=1}^{N_x-1}\sum_{j=0}^{N_y-1}a_{i,j+1/2}D_yv_{i,j+1/2}D_yw_{i,j+1/2}\right).
$$
The homogeneous scheme solves $A_h^av=f_h$ in $I_h$ with $v=0$ on the boundary. For Dirichlet data $g$, it solves the same interior equations with $v=g$ at boundary nodes. This definition specifies the rectangular Dirichlet stencil; it does not specify a Neumann or nonrectangular boundary closure.

On the grid of [[def-rectangular-grid-and-dirichlet-flux-stencil]], put $q^x_{i+1/2,j}=a_{i+1/2,j}D_xv_{i+1/2,j}$ and $q^y_{i,j+1/2}=a_{i,j+1/2}D_yv_{i,j+1/2}$. For any grid functions $v,w$,
$$
\langle A_h^av,w\rangle_h=E_h^a(v,w)-h_y\sum_{j=1}^{N_y-1}\left(q^x_{N_x-1/2,j}w_{N_x,j}-q^x_{1/2,j}w_{0,j}\right)-h_x\sum_{i=1}^{N_x-1}\left(q^y_{i,N_y-1/2}w_{i,N_y}-q^y_{i,1/2}w_{i,0}\right).
$$
In particular, if $w$ vanishes on the boundary, then $\langle A_h^av,w\rangle_h=E_h^a(v,w)$. For every $v\in X_{h,0}$,
$$
\|v\|_h^2\le L_x^2\,h_xh_y\sum_{j=1}^{N_y-1}\sum_{i=0}^{N_x-1}|D_xv_{i+1/2,j}|^2.
$$
If all horizontal and vertical face values satisfy $a_{i+1/2,j},a_{i,j+1/2}\ge a_0>0$, then the homogeneous Dirichlet matrix $A_h^a$ is invertible and
$$
\|(A_h^a)^{-1}\|_{\ell_h^2\to\ell_h^2}\le \frac{L_x^2}{a_0},
$$
where $\ell_h^2$ is the norm $\|\cdot\|_h$ on interior vectors. The constants are independent of $N_x,N_y$.

Fix a dimension $d\ge1$, side lengths $L_j>0$, integers $N_j\ge2$, directional diffusivities $\kappa_j>0$, and spacings $h_j=L_j/N_j$. For a finite periodic rectangular grid let
$$
G_h^{\rm per}=\prod_{j=1}^d(\mathbb Z/N_j\mathbb Z),\qquad \langle v,w\rangle_h=\Bigl(\prod_{j=1}^d h_j\Bigr)\sum_{i\in G_h^{\rm per}}v_iw_i,
$$
and define the positive centered heat operator, with indices reduced modulo $N_j$, by
$$(A_h^{\rm per}v)_i=\sum_{j=1}^d\kappa_j\frac{2v_i-v_{i+e_j}-v_{i-e_j}}{h_j^2}.$$

For a two-dimensional Dirichlet rectangle, use the nodes and weighted interior inner product of [[def-rectangular-grid-and-dirichlet-flux-stencil]]. At an interior node $(i,j)$ define
$$(A_h^{B}V)_{ij}=\kappa_x\frac{2V_{ij}-V_{i+1,j}-V_{i-1,j}}{h_x^2}+\kappa_y\frac{2V_{ij}-V_{i,j+1}-V_{i,j-1}}{h_y^2},$$
where values on boundary neighbours are the prescribed Dirichlet row $B$. Write $A_h^0$ for the square matrix on interior values when the boundary is zero. For any boundary vector $B$, let $c_h(B)$ be the result of applying this stencil to the grid vector that equals $B$ on the boundary and $0$ at interior nodes. Then $A_h^B V=A_h^0V+c_h(B)$ on interior nodes.

Let $T>0$, an integer $M\ge1$, $\Delta t=T/M$, $t_n=n\Delta t$, and $\theta\in[0,1]$. Given interior initial data $U^0$, interior source samples $F^n$, and, in the Dirichlet case, boundary rows $B^n$ for $0\le n\le M$ whose time-zero row agrees with the initial grid data, the periodic update is
$$
\frac{U^{n+1}-U^n}{\Delta t}+A_h^{\rm per}\bigl((1-\theta)U^n+\theta U^{n+1}\bigr)=(1-\theta)F^n+\theta F^{n+1},\quad 0\le n<M.
$$
The Dirichlet update, with the boundary values imposed at every time level, is
$$
\frac{U^{n+1}-U^n}{\Delta t}+A_h^0\bigl((1-\theta)U^n+\theta U^{n+1}\bigr)=(1-\theta)\bigl(F^n-c_h(B^n)\bigr)+\theta\bigl(F^{n+1}-c_h(B^{n+1})\bigr),\quad 0\le n<M.
$$
Thus the interior rows use the exact boundary contributions at both endpoints of the time step. The choices $\theta=0,1/2,1$ are forward Euler, Crank–Nicolson, and backward Euler applied to the spatially semidiscrete heat equation; this definition does not redefine those ODE time-stepping procedures.

For a homogeneous-source update with periodic rows or zero Dirichlet boundary values, let $Q_h$ be its one-step linear map when that step is well defined, and give it the operator norm induced by $\|\cdot\|_h$. The family is **grid-norm power stable on $[0,T]$** if there is $C_T<\infty$, independent of the grid and time step, such that $\|Q_h^n\|_{h\to h}\le C_T$ whenever $n\Delta t\le T$. This is a statement in the mesh-dependent finite grid norms defined above.

derivations.claim: By [F3] the step has a unique solution. Write $\delta U=U^{n+1}-U^n$. The identity $U_\theta=U^n+\theta\delta U$ gives $\langle\delta U,U_\theta\rangle_h=\frac12(\|U^{n+1}\|_h^2-\|U^n\|_h^2)+(\theta-\tfrac12)\|\delta U\|_h^2$ by expanding the two squared norms.

The two terms after the norm difference on the left are nonnegative by $\theta\ge1/2$ and [F2]. Cauchy–Schwarz and the triangle inequality give $|\langle q^n,U_\theta\rangle_h|\le\|q^n\|_h\|U_\theta\|_h\le\|q^n\|_h\max(\|U^n\|_h,\|U^{n+1}\|_h)$.

citations.quote:
Fix a dimension $d\ge1$, side lengths $L_j>0$, integers $N_j\ge2$, directional diffusivities $\kappa_j>0$, and spacings $h_j=L_j/N_j$. For a finite periodic rectangular grid let
$$
G_h^{\rm per}=\prod_{j=1}^d(\mathbb Z/N_j\mathbb Z),\qquad \langle v,w\rangle_h=\Bigl(\prod_{j=1}^d h_j\Bigr)\sum_{i\in G_h^{\rm per}}v_iw_i,
$$
and define the positive centered heat operator, with indices reduced modulo $N_j$, by
$$(A_h^{\rm per}v)_i=\sum_{j=1}^d\kappa_j\frac{2v_i-v_{i+e_j}-v_{i-e_j}}{h_j^2}.$$

For a two-dimensional Dirichlet rectangle, use the nodes and weighted interior inner product of [[def-rectangular-grid-and-dirichlet-flux-stencil]]. At an interior node $(i,j)$ define
$$(A_h^{B}V)_{ij}=\kappa_x\frac{2V_{ij}-V_{i+1,j}-V_{i-1,j}}{h_x^2}+\kappa_y\frac{2V_{ij}-V_{i,j+1}-V_{i,j-1}}{h_y^2},$$
where values on boundary neighbours are the prescribed Dirichlet row $B$. Write $A_h^0$ for the square matrix on interior values when the boundary is zero. For any boundary vector $B$, let $c_h(B)$ be the result of applying this stencil to the grid vector that equals $B$ on the boundary and $0$ at interior nodes. Then $A_h^B V=A_h^0V+c_h(B)$ on interior nodes.

Let $T>0$, an integer $M\ge1$, $\Delta t=T/M$, $t_n=n\Delta t$, and $\theta\in[0,1]$. Given interior initial data $U^0$, interior source samples $F^n$, and, in the Dirichlet case, boundary rows $B^n$ for $0\le n\le M$ whose time-zero row agrees with the initial grid data, the periodic update is
$$
\frac{U^{n+1}-U^n}{\Delta t}+A_h^{\rm per}\bigl((1-\theta)U^n+\theta U^{n+1}\bigr)=(1-\theta)F^n+\theta F^{n+1},\quad 0\le n<M.
$$
The Dirichlet update, with the boundary values imposed at every time level, is
$$
\frac{U^{n+1}-U^n}{\Delta t}+A_h^0\bigl((1-\theta)U^n+\theta U^{n+1}\bigr)=(1-\theta)\bigl(F^n-c_h(B^n)\bigr)+\theta\bigl(F^{n+1}-c_h(B^{n+1})\bigr),\quad 0\le n<M.
$$
Thus the interior rows use the exact boundary contributions at both endpoints of the time step. The choices $\theta=0,1/2,1$ are forward Euler, Crank–Nicolson, and backward Euler applied to the spatially semidiscrete heat equation; this definition does not redefine those ODE time-stepping procedures.

For a homogeneous-source update with periodic rows or zero Dirichlet boundary values, let $Q_h$ be its one-step linear map when that step is well defined, and give it the operator norm induced by $\|\cdot\|_h$. The family is **grid-norm power stable on $[0,T]$** if there is $C_T<\infty$, independent of the grid and time step, such that $\|Q_h^n\|_{h\to h}\le C_T$ whenever $n\Delta t\le T$. This is a statement in the mesh-dependent finite grid norms defined above.

On the finite two-dimensional rectangular Dirichlet grid of [[def-parabolic-theta-finite-difference-scheme]], suppose $\theta\in[0,1]$, the source is zero, and
$$
\Delta t(1-\theta)\left(\frac{\kappa_x}{h_x^2}+\frac{\kappa_y}{h_y^2}\right)\le\frac12.
$$
Then every numerical interior value at every time level lies between the minimum and maximum of all initial and prescribed boundary values. In particular, with homogeneous boundary rows and $\theta=1/2$, this maximum-principle condition is $\Delta t(\kappa_x/h_x^2+\kappa_y/h_y^2)\le1$, a stricter sufficient condition than the unconditional weighted $L^2$ stability for the same homogeneous problem proved in [[thm-parabolic-theta-l2-stability-for-half-theta]].

derivations.claim: Direct differentiation gives $u_t=-2\pi^2u$ and $\Delta u=-2\pi^2u$, so $u_t-\Delta u=0$. Also $u=0$ on the four sides and $u(x,y,0)=\sin(\pi x)\sin(\pi y)\in[0,1]$.
On $[0,1]$, $0\le\sin(\pi x),\sin(\pi y)\le1$, and for $t\ge0$ the factor $e^{-2\pi^2t}$ lies in $(0,1]$. The explicit formula therefore gives $0\le u\le1$ throughout the closed cylinder.

The sampled initial values lie in $[0,1]$ and the boundary rows are zero. With $\theta=0$ and $\kappa_x=\kappa_y=1$, the condition in [F2] is exactly $2\Delta t/h^2\le1/2$. Therefore [F2] gives $0\le U^n_{ij}\le1$ at every grid node and time level.
